option.name: content
option.value:
# Standards for Commit Messages --- ## General Guidelines - Use the imperative mood in commit messages (e.g., "Fix bug" instead of "Fixed bug" or "Fixes bug"). - Keep the subject line concise (50 characters or less) and provide a detailed description in the body if necessary. - Separate the subject from the body with a blank line. - Use the body to explain what and why, not how. - Limit lines in the body to 72 characters for better readability. - Reference relevant issues or pull requests in the commit message when applicable. - Use consistent formatting for commit messages across the project. - Avoid using vague terms like "fix", "update", or "change" without context. - Proofread commit messages for clarity and correctness before finalising. - If the commit is associated with an Azure DevOps work item, always start the commit message with the work item ID, then a space, then the message (e.g., "CP-XXXXX Example message"). - The Azure DevOps work item ID will often be found in the branch name, e.g., in `feature/CP-XXXXX-add-new-api-endpoint`, the work item ID is `CP-XXXXX`. - For commits that are not associated with a work item (such as automated commits, dependency updates, or minor documentation fixes), the work item ID is not required. In these cases, start the commit message directly with the summary. - Australian or American English spelling is acceptable.
## Example Commit Message Structure ``` CP-XXXXX Short (50 chars or less) summary of changes
Detailed explanation of the changes, if necessary. This can span multiple lines and should provide context for the changes made. Limit lines to 72 characters in this section. See related Pull Requests: #123, #456 ```
